info.name: Atlas API (v0.0.0)
info.description: Atlas authentication & user management API. Generated from the code-derived OpenAPI document (the same one served at /v1/openapi.json) by scripts/gen-postman.mjs. Import this collection, import the environment template, set `baseUrl` and your keys, and every request is pre-wired with auth, path/query params, and a body example.

item.name: POST Meter usage against a key's spend caps, atomically. Body: amount (positive integer), unit (app-defined, e.g. reques

request.description:
Meter usage against a key's spend caps, atomically. Body: amount (positive integer), unit (app-defined, e.g. requests or usd_cents), optional idempotency_key. When the debit fits every cap for that unit it is recorded (day, month and total counters) and allowed:true is returned; when it would exceed a cap — or is larger than a per-request cap — NOTHING is recorded and the response is 200 with allowed:false and code LIMIT_EXCEEDED, so you enforce it in your own transaction. Concurrent debits on one key serialize: two can never both pass a cap only one fits under. Day and month windows are UTC calendar windows. The same idempotency_key (kept 24 hours) returns the first outcome without counting again (idempotent_replay:true); reusing it with a different unit or amount is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. A revoked or expired key is 409 CONFLICT; an unknown id 404. The first time a cap fills or refuses a debit in a window, api_key.limit_reached is emitted (once per cap per window).
**Required scope:** `api_keys:write`

`POST /v1/api_keys/{id}/usage`

item.name: POST Mint a short-lived, JWKS-signed access JWT (token_use:api_key, jti) whose exp is clamped to the smallest of the req

request.description:
Mint a short-lived, JWKS-signed access JWT (token_use:api_key, jti) whose exp is clamped to the smallest of the request, the key expiry and the org ceiling; scopes + constraints are embedded so a resource verifies it OFFLINE against the instance JWKS. When the key registered a public_key, the token also carries cnf.jkt (proof-of-possession) and a resource additionally checks a holder-signed proof. Authenticate with (1) an sk_ bearer + the ak_ in the body, (2) an Authorization: Bearer ak_… that self-mints for itself, or (3) no bearer + x-publishable-key naming the instance with the ak_ in the body. A key only ever mints within its own instance. The api_keys:read scope applies ONLY to the sk_ path; the ak_ and publishable-key paths are self-scoped.
**Required scope:** `api_keys:read`

`POST /v1/api_keys/token`

item.name: POST Mint an end-user API key for a user, organization or machine (returns the ak_ secret once), OR import an existing k

request.description:
Mint an end-user API key for a user, organization or machine (returns the ak_ secret once), OR import an existing key by its SHA-256 hash (hash_algorithm "sha256" or "sha256_hex") so it verifies against the original secret. Normally authenticated with an sk_ key; a LAN/offline MACHINE may instead self-provision a key for ITSELF by presenting Authorization: Bearer <machine JWT> (token_use:m2m from /v1/machines/token) + x-publishable-key — the subject is forced to that machine and it cannot grant itself management-plane scopes. Pass public_key (an SPKI PEM) to make the key proof-of-possession: tokens minted from it carry cnf.jkt and a resource verifies a holder-signed proof OFFLINE. Pass limits (an array of { unit, amount, period } with period request|day|month|total) to set per-key spend caps, metered with POST /v1/api_keys/{id}/usage. Key controls: enabled (false = minted disabled), rate_limit { max, window_seconds } (per-key verify throttle), remaining (a use budget each successful verify spends), prefix (a custom secret prefix such as acme, giving acme_<id>_<secret>), and expires_in_seconds as an alternative to expires_at. The instance expiry policy (endUserApiKeys.defaultExpiresInSeconds / maxExpiresInSeconds) gives a key sent without an expiry the default lifetime and refuses one longer than the ceiling (400). Emits api_key.created (on mint, import and machine self-provisioning).
**Required scope:** `api_keys:write`

`POST /v1/api_keys`

item.name: POST Verify a presented end-user API key secret. Any secret works: a natively minted ak_ key AND an imported key of any

request.description:
Verify a presented end-user API key secret. Any secret works: a natively minted ak_ key AND an imported key of any format or prefix (resolved by its SHA-256). Returns the subject, name, claims, scopes, constraints, spend caps (limits) and their current-window usage, or valid:false alone (unknown, revoked, expired, disabled or subject deleted; never says which). Send required_scopes to require scopes the key must carry. A live key refused by its own policy answers valid:false with a code: insufficient_scope (missing_scopes), rate_limited (retry_after_ms, from the key rate_limit) or usage_exhausted (no remaining uses left). Each successful verify spends one remaining use, atomically. Rate-limited.
**Required scope:** `api_keys:read`

`POST /v1/api_keys/verify`

Returns 201 with the full custom_domain object — including its `id` (dom_…), which you pass to POST /v1/domains/{id}/verify once DNS is published — plus the CNAME `instructions` to follow (or a `note` for a platform subdomain, which is live immediately). Pass `dns: {provider: "cloudflare", api_token}` and Atlas writes the CNAME itself: it finds the zone, creates the record DNS-only (never proxied; `dns.proxied: true` is refused), waits briefly for it to resolve and verifies, so the domain can go from nothing to active in one call (`verified` in the response; otherwise call verify later). The token is stored encrypted and is never readable back (the response shows only `dns.provider` and `token_set`). An existing record that points elsewhere is not overwritten unless `dns.overwrite` is true (409 DNS_RECORD_CONFLICT); a rejected token is 422 DNS_TOKEN_REJECTED; no visible zone is 422 DNS_ZONE_NOT_FOUND.
**Required scope:** `domains:write`

`POST /v1/domains`

Setting the retired raw branding fields (branding.customCss / customHtmlHeader / customHtmlFooter) returns 422 naming the field — use the design settings (PUT /v1/instance/design) instead; clearing them (null or "") is accepted. request.description:
Rotate the instance signing key, optionally switching its algorithm (`alg`: RS256 or ES256; RS256 is the default for new instances). A new key signs from now on, and a secondary key (for APIs set to the other algorithm) rotates with it; the previous public key stays in the JWKS for `grace_period_seconds` (default 86400, at most 2592000) so issued tokens and relying-party JWKS caches keep verifying. A second rotation inside a running grace window is a 409 unless `emergency: true`, which publishes ONLY the new key (every token signed by the old one stops verifying at once — for a suspected compromise). request.description:
Bring your own key: keep the signing key in AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS or Azure Key Vault. Atlas validates the settings, reads (or creates) a key version, proves it can sign with it, saves the settings (credentials encrypted under the instance key) and rotates the main signing key to it — the previous key stays published for `grace_period_seconds` unless `emergency`. From then on every token is signed by the KMS (the private key never leaves it), the JWKS publishes its public key, and POST /v1/instance/signing_keys/rotate creates a new key version there. item.name: POST Managed email: Atlas sets up your sending domain (the domain of `from_address`) on YOUR OWN Resend or Brevo account

request.description:
Managed email: Atlas sets up your sending domain (the domain of `from_address`) on YOUR OWN Resend or Brevo account, with your API key, and sends through it once the domain is verified. Pass `transport` ("resend" | "brevo") with `config.api_key`, or `provider_id` of your configured Resend or Brevo email provider; without either the call is refused with 422 (param `config.api_key`). The key is stored, write-only, as the instance's email provider in `managed_domain` mode. Returns 201 with the DNS `records` to publish (DKIM, SPF / return-path for Resend; ownership, DKIM, DMARC for Brevo). Until the domain is verified email delivery stays unavailable and preflight warns `managed_email_unverified`. Pass `dns: {provider: "cloudflare", api_token}` and Atlas writes the records itself (DNS-only; the token is write-only) and verifies in the same call when DNS propagates in time. Atlas also registers a bounce / complaint webhook on your Resend or Brevo account, for this instance only (`feedback_webhook`); the counts appear in `usage`. No Atlas sending limits apply (`limits: null`): the account and its limits are yours. Atlas never uses an email account of its own. 409 when the domain is set up on another Atlas instance; 502 MANAGED_EMAIL_PROVIDER_ERROR when your provider refuses.
**Required scope:** `messaging:write`

`POST /v1/messaging_providers/email/managed`

item.name: POST Put your OWN email provider in development mode, so a development instance can send sign-in email without a verifie

request.description:
Put your OWN email provider in development mode, so a development instance can send sign-in email without a verified domain: Resend's `onboarding@resend.dev` (the default From for Resend; Resend delivers it only to your Resend account's own address), or a single sender address your provider has verified (Brevo, SES, SMTP, a Mailgun sandbox). Body: `provider_id` of your configured email provider, or `transport` + `config` (+ `from_address`) exactly as PUT /v1/messaging_providers/email; with neither, 422 (param `provider_id`). Only Atlas's own sign-in emails are sent (verification code, magic link, password reset, password changed, account exists notice, organization invitation); every subject starts with "[Atlas test] " and every message ends with a development footer; template overrides and branding are not used and custom notification templates are refused. Capped per instance per day and per recipient per hour (`limits`); over a cap a send is refused with 429 DEVELOPMENT_EMAIL_LIMIT_REACHED. The instance then counts as able to deliver email, and preflight warns `email_development_sender`. Atlas never sends with an account of its own. 201 when the mode is turned on, 200 when it already was. 409 DEVELOPMENT_EMAIL_NOT_ALLOWED on a production instance.
**Required scope:** `messaging:write`

item.name: POST Keep a session alive from your backend: slides its inactivity (idle) window as if the user had just loaded a page.

request.description:
Keep a session alive from your backend: slides its inactivity (idle) window as if the user had just loaded a page. Use it when your app mounts the Atlas SDK only on some pages, so time spent on pages without it does not count as inactivity. Never extends past the session's absolute expiry and never revives an ended session — a revoked session is 409 SESSION_REVOKED, a session that already timed out is 409 SESSION_IDLE_EXPIRED, and one past its absolute expiry is 409 SESSION_EXPIRED; an unknown id is 404. At most one effective write per minute per session: a touch within 60 seconds of the session's last activity returns the current state with extended:false, so calling it on every request is safe. No request body. Returns the session with last_active_at and idle_expires_at.
**Required scope:** `sessions:write`

`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/touch`

The data is returned on the session object and on the Frontend API client session, and — when the instance sets session.customData.inToken — in the next session token under session.customData.claim, so it never shadows a reserved claim. Rotate the endpoint signing secret. The new secret is revealed exactly once. By default (`overlap_seconds` 0) the old secret stops signing at once. With `overlap_seconds` (at most 604800 = 7 days) every delivery carries two signatures in `atlas-signature` (`v1,<new> v1,<old>`, the new one first), so a verifier holding either secret passes while you deploy the new one; after that only the new secret signs. **Required scope:** `webhooks:write`

Atlas registers it there (events email.bounced and email.complained) when a Resend managed domain is set up or verified, and keeps the signing secret Resend returns, encrypted. Verifies the Svix signature (svix-id, svix-timestamp, svix-signature; 5-minute tolerance) over the raw body with that instance's secret. item.name: POST Two-way referral sync: the instance's referral platform reports referral changes made after sign-up (voided, approv

request.description:
Two-way referral sync: the instance's referral platform reports referral changes made after sign-up (voided, approved, paused, reassigned, or a referral created later). Referalli signs with its webhook endpoint's own secret (Standard Webhooks: webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature); the Atlas referral protocol signs like Atlas webhooks (atlas-id, atlas-timestamp, atlas-signature) with the inbound secret, or the connection's signing secret when none is set. 5-minute tolerance. The change lands on the user's referral (matched by customerRef, else by the platform's referral id) and fires user.updated. Events Atlas does not act on, unknown customers and out-of-order events are a 200 that changes nothing; a bad signature is a 401; 404 when referrals are off or the provider sends no events.

`POST /v1/webhooks/referrals/{instanceId}`
